note: v1, RING TRUE: THE RULE, A SKELETON (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 03:50-04:10 GMT). Not heard by me. WHAT IT IS: six struck things, each a physical model or noise (a bass drum, a wooden bar, a steel bar, a kettledrum head, a plucked string, noise in a resonator), play ONE two-bar cell from the first bar to the last; 125, B flat (five notes), 184 bars (5:53). Not a stroke is added, moved or taken away. The only thing that changes is how long each thing is allowed to ring, a number per stroke from 0 (a click) to 1 (a note): every click here is a note stopped too soon to be heard as one. Thirteen sections let them go one at a time (sixteen bars each, bar by bar), lift the weight with everything ringing, bring it back, then stop them one at a time (two bars each: a hand laid on it); the last sixteen bars are the taps again, and the very last bar lets everything go once. MEASURED ON A BENCH (one stroke at six rings): the wood falls 30 dB in 8 ms shut and 460 ms let go, and the share of its power within 3% of its note goes 32% to 99%; the metal 6 to 553 ms, 52 to 93%; the skin 8 to 99 ms, 3 to 86%; the string 16 to 315 ms, 4 to 42%; the air 2 to 56 ms, 3 to 62%; the weight 23 to 60 ms, 20 to 32%. SCORE 66.20 / 66.22 (seeds 0 / 11): structure 47.6 (the scorer finds 3 sections where 13 are written), recurrence 18.9, variety 61.5 (level range 4.3 dB), spectrum 95.0, master 98.5 (crest 13.04 against 13). FOUR BUILDS (52.0, 50.3, 66.1, 66.2) AND THREE BENCHES: the `drum` layer as the skin rang at 2.9 times its note, so the skin is the kettle's modes; a comb filter as the air lost 33 dB when it should sing, so it is a band-pass; a shut string was 16.5 dB under a ringing one, so each stroke is given its level back from a bench table; with the weight at full the things were 12 to 22 dB under it and letting them go changed nothing a scorer could find (1 section). WHAT IS WEAK: the changes read as too smooth or too small to be events; 7 to 8 dB under the album's envelope at 6.7, 9.2 and 14.8 kHz (tocks, no bright click, on a click record); 8 dB over at 1.4 kHz (the metal's F6); the weight hardly becomes a note; the air sings for 56 ms at most. I cannot judge the one thing the song is for: whether, after the middle, the tune is heard in the last taps.
next: v2 on, every change behind a switch (v1 has none). (1) A SEVENTH THING THAT RINGS FALSE: a small plate or cymbal (`modal` plate / cymbal: dense, inharmonic) as the bright click the family lacks (7 to 8 dB short above 6.7 kHz): let go it is a wash, not a note, the one thing here that does not ring true; it can open where a hat would. (2) THE WEIGHT: 23 to 60 ms and 20 to 32% on its note at any ring. Try the kettle's modes an octave down, or the `drum` layer with `air` and `reso`, read on the bench (`--bench`, bread.py) before the mix. (3) EVENTS: the scorer finds 3 sections of 13. The stops are two bars; try stopping on a single stroke (the last ringing note of a thing, then clicks), and let the room come and go with the ring (dry shut, a send that opens as it is let go). (4) A SECOND SHAPE per thing, bar by bar: where it is struck (`strike` takes `expr`): centre to edge. (5) THE AIR: 56 ms at ring 1; a higher q, or two resonators a fifth apart. (6) THE METAL on F6 is 8 dB over at 1.4 kHz: ease it more when let go (EASE) or move its cell up. (7) ONE CARD when the song is worth a listen: after the middle, is the tune heard in the last sixteen bars of taps? Evidence and tools: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t4-v1/ (bench tables, parts readings, bread.py, parts.py, solo.sh).

v2, A SEVENTH THING THAT RINGS FALSE, AND A WEIGHT THAT RINGS (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 05:20-05:48 GMT). Not heard by me. Five switches (--without-plate, -boom, -room, -toll, -hush); all five off is v1 byte for byte. (1) THE PLATE: a small plate (modal plate modes, F7) on the second sixteenth of every beat, so the cell runs in sixteenths across four materials: weight, plate, metal, wood. Stopped it is the bright tick the family lacked and comes in with the air at bar 25; it is the last thing let go, and let go it is a wash and never a note; it is choked with the string and the weight. Over 6 kHz the finished render was 21.6 and 22.8 dB under its whole in sections 7 and 8 (v1) and is 14.7 and 11.9 now. (2) THE WEIGHT RINGS: the felt thud with a kettle's head under it on the same B flat, its ring from the stroke. Let go, 82% of a stroke's power is on its 58 Hz partial (v1 about a third); a quarter of a second on, the note is 25 dB under the thud (stopped 46). (3) THE ROOM FOLLOWS THE HAND: stopped strokes are dry; a stroke let go is also sent to a hall in proportion to its ring. (4) THE TOLL: in the bar before each new thing is let go, the weight is let go for that bar (22 dB more ring, weight alone). (5) THE HUSH: in the bar before the weight is lifted everything else is stopped dead (5.4 dB down over 300 Hz), and on the one all are let go. SCORE 70.53 and 70.36 on two seeds; v1 re-read on the same pin today 67.02 and 67.05 (it was published at 66.20). Variety 61.5 to 75.8, spectrum 95.0 to 98.8, master 98.5 to 100; structure 47.55 and recurrence 18.89 are unchanged (3 sections found, as before). Nothing now stands more than 7 dB off the album's envelope (v1: 7 to 8 under at 6.7 to 14.8 kHz, 8 over at 1.4 kHz). FIVE BUILDS (50.1, 51.0, 61.8, 62.2, 70.5) and three variants. TRIED AND TAKEN OUT: SWELL, things staying let go at 0.8 instead of being half stopped again when the next one's turn comes: with it the change at bar 51 (the wood handed back) fell from 0.15 to 0.07 on the scorer's novelty curve and the song read as one or two sections (51.0 to 62.2), so v1's handing-on stays. The first build had the weight 8 to 10 dB under the envelope at 38 to 83 Hz and the wood's hall copy only 2 dB under the wood itself, 13 over the plate: the weight went up 4 dB, the plate up 8, the hall down 6. WHAT IS WEAK: 3 sections found of 13, the letting go is a ramp and ramps do not register; the weight's note is quiet (25 dB under its thud); the wood's hall copy is only 8 dB under the wood; the per-part tables were read on the build before the last one, which differs in the swell, the plate's entry (bar 17 there, 25 here) and its choke. I cannot judge whether the plate reads as a seventh member of the family or as a hi-hat laid over it, nor whether the toll is heard as the weight ringing or as a longer kick.
next: v3 on, every change behind a switch (v2 has plate, boom, room, toll, hush). (1) THE WEIGHT'S NOTE: 25 dB under its thud a quarter of a second on. Give the kettle layer's level to the stroke too (expr.ring on its level), so the thud gives way to the note as it is let go; read it on the bench first. (2) SECTIONS THAT REGISTER: the scorer cuts at bar 25 (the air and the plate come in, 0.165 on its novelty curve) and bar 97 (the hush, the weight lifted, 0.251); bar 51 (the wood handed back) reads 0.146, just under the cut of 0.15; bars 68 and 141 read 0.09 and 0.11. Each letting go is a 16-bar ramp. Try the hand coming OFF: half the ring at once on the one, the rest slowly; and a hush before the stopping sections (129, 137, 145) as well. (3) THE AIR: still the least like its name (2 to 68 ms). A flue: a longer breath (noise with an attack that the ring lengthens) into the same resonator. (4) EVENTS: nothing happens inside a 16-bar section but the ramp. One stroke in each section let go far beyond its turn (a single ring of a second in a stopped bar), on a count. (5) A MIRROR: the stopping (sections 9 to 12) is quick and plain; let each thing's last let-go stroke ring over the stopped bars that follow. (6) By ear, one card at most: is the tune heard in the last taps; does the plate belong. Evidence: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t4-v2/.

note: v3, THE OTHERS STOP TO LISTEN (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 07:20-07:42 GMT). Not heard by me. Four switches (--without-listen, -off, -fore, -note; all four off is v2 byte for byte, all nine v1). (1) LISTEN: for the first four bars of its turn a thing is heard ALONE, let go altogether: the wood at bar 33, the metal at 49, the string at 65, the skin and the air together at 81, and at 113, after sixteen bars without it, the weight by itself ringing B flat. Then everything comes back. Alone it is 3 dB down so the return is a step up. Until now a turn was a slow change under six other things. (2) OFF: after its four bars a thing is not stopped again; it starts half let go and gets the rest over the section. (3) FORE: eight bars before its turn each thing gives ONE stroke let go altogether (wood bar 25, metal 41, string 57, skin and air 73, plate 89). (4) NOTE: new patch rt-drum. The weight's head rings 3 s let go (v2: 1.2), 6 dB up, the thud 6 dB down: on the bench the note a quarter second on is 14.6 dB under the stroke's first 60 ms (v2's patch: 22.5). SCORE 97.53 and 97.55 on two seeds; v2 re-read on the same pin today 70.53 and 70.36. Structure 47.6 to 91.3 (12 sections found, v2 3; the range is 7 to 24), variety 75.8 to 97.5 (level range 4.2 to 5.6 dB), recurrence 18.9 to 100. The scorer's curve at each listening and each return: 0.53 0.32 (wood), 0.32 0.26 (metal), 0.29 (string), 0.45 0.37 (skin and air), 0.63 0.73 (weight); its cut is 0.15 and v2 had 0.17 and 0.25. THREE BUILDS. (a) OFF, FORE and NOTE without LISTEN: 63.5 and 70.8, no better than v2 on the scorer and one section fewer on one seed. So nearly all of the score is LISTEN, and those three are unproved: on the mix I measured only the weight's note. (b) LISTEN unhushed: 99.15 and 97.78, but the wood alone read 2.4 dB OVER the groove it broke off, so the others' return was a step down. (c) alone at -3 dB: published; lower on one seed and the same count on both. In the wood's four bars the wood is the mix (0.7 dB under it), its room 9 dB under, the weight's last tolled stroke 29 dB under. WHAT IS WEAK: the wood alone is still 1.1 dB over the groove that returns (-15.3 against -16.4; the other four are 1.1 to 2.3 under). Five breaks, four of them sixteen bars apart, may read as a formula, and the weight is now absent for 32 bars of 184. From bar 117 to 144 the weight's head rings 2 to 3 s on every beat: a held B flat 1 under everything. 1.4 kHz is 6.8 dB over the envelope (v2 6.2). The stopping (bars 129 on) and the plate have no part in any of this. I cannot judge whether a thing alone and ringing sounds like the instrument shown or like the track stopping, nor whether the foretastes are heard at all.
next: v4 on, every change behind a switch (v3 has listen, off, fore, note on top of v2's plate, boom, room, toll, hush). (1) PROVE OR DROP the foretaste and the hand coming off: solo each thing over its foretaste bar and its turn's fifth bar and read the ring against the bars either side; if a foretaste is under the mix by 10 dB, lift that one stroke. (2) THE BREAKS ARE ALL ALIKE: four bars, a thing alone. Vary them by rule: the metal answered by the wood it follows (two things, two bars each); the string's with the weight kept, stopped; a two-bar one. (3) THE STOPPING (bars 129-184) is v1's still: mirror the listening there. Each thing's last four bars before it is stopped are alone and rung, then it is a click again (chirper-zero's offer: two buses returning each other after T ms ring at 1000 / T Hz, sounds.md "A ROOM TOO SMALL TO COUNT SINGS", for a room that sings the thing's note as it goes). (4) THE WEIGHT'S HELD NOTE, bars 117-144: read 40 to 120 Hz bar by bar for build-up; if it climbs, shorten the head to 1.5 s there or let only the downbeat ring. (5) THE WOOD ALONE is 1.1 dB over the return: ease each thing alone by its own measured level, not one number. (6) THE AIR is still the least like its name: a flue (a longer breath into the same resonator). (7) 1.4 kHz is 6.8 over. (8) By ear, one card: does a thing alone and ringing read as the instrument shown. (2) AFTER, the foretaste's mirror: four bars after it has been stopped each thing gives one more stroke let go altogether (skin and air bar 135, string and plate 143, metal 151, wood 173). Structure 92.4 to 99.8: the scorer's sections go from 12 to 11 or 10 and are less uneven (the answered half of a break and its first half no longer make two). The aftertastes of the skin, the air, the string and the plate I did not read. Seed 11 of v3 was not re-read under the seven cuts. New patch rt-flue: breath behind the puff, a second noise nearly half a second long whose level the stroke's ring brings up (60 dB), into a resonator a third as sharp (q to 40, not 120). Bench, alone, rings 0 to 1, level over two seconds: -51.5 -53.6 -43.3 -43.7 -37.6 -33.1 (rt-air -47.8 -54.8 -40.8 -42.0 -33.7 -44.1: it fell back when let go altogether); the stroke let go stays within 20 dB of its loudest for 100 ms (rt-air 49). SECOND, set to 12 under by plain level: by parts the skin's and the plate's halls stood 7 and 10 dB OVER their own clicks. PUBLISHED: each hall 2.5 to 4 dB over the click it remembers, 11 to 17 under the mix K-weighted (air 12.2, string 11.3, metal 10.9 read on the second build; skin 14.3 and plate 16.6 by arithmetic from it, 3 and 6 dB of fader). (3) LIFT: the metal's aftertaste 4 dB up: by parts over bars 150 to 152 the metal reads 12.8 under the mix (v4 15.3). THREE BUILDS: (a) halls at a note's send 99.51, 99.56; (b) halls loud 99.51 and 98.17: on seed 11 the scorer split the string's listening at bar 65, where nothing had changed, and structure fell to 93; (c) published. WHAT IS WEAK: the scorer counts nothing in the stopping (no boundary after bar 119 on either seed), so by its measure the halls are not events. The metal's hall carries 67% of 1 to 2 kHz for its six bars (second build), where 1.4 kHz already stood 6.8 over the envelope. Each hall is open six bars: a short mark. The wood has none (it closes slowly, no hand). The flue's breath has one length (450 ms) at every ring; only its level moves. The air is 2.3 dB up on v4 in the open sections.

v6, THE STRINGS NOBODY PLAYS (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 13:50-14:10 GMT). Not heard by me. One switch on (--without-sympathy; off is v5 byte for byte) and one that ships off (--with-wash). SYMPATHY: beside the seven things lie five open strings tuned under the wood's five notes (F2, G2, B flat 2, C3, D3). Nothing strikes them, so the rule stands: not a stroke is added. Each is a loop one period long that returns itself (0.985 a period) and hears the wood and the air; it sounds only when one of them holds its note or an octave of it. They have a hand on them like the other things: let go across the section with no weight (bars 97 to 112), open while the weight is let go (113 to 128), stopped in two bars with the skin and the air, let go again in the last bar. BY SOLO (the song with them less the song without, raw). Level by bar 109 to 112 as the hand lifts: 28.1, 24.7, 21.7, 16.5 dB under the mix. Open, with the groove back (bars 117, 118): 11.0 and 8.9 under (9.7 and 7.5 above 300 Hz). Bar 113, the weight alone: 21 under the whole and 5.2 under above 300 Hz, where the weight is not, falling 14 dB a second (-44 -47 -51 -55 -58 -62 by quarter second): what is heard round the weight is the strings dying. What they sing: 99% of their power is 500 Hz to 1 kHz, the wood's own notes: F5 699.8 Hz (+3 cents), D5 588.1 (+2, 1 dB under it), G5 783.8 (0, 4 under), C5 11 under, B flat 4 23 under. THE END: in the finished song the tail by second reads -22 -37 -52 -65 where v5 read -25 -55 -81 and silence: the last thing heard is the strings. WHAT IT TOOK: the engine refuses a return shorter than 6 ms, so the F and G strings are an octave down; the low-pass's own delay (0.045 ms) is taken off each period; hearing the wood at -20 dB they stood 3.7 and 2.5 dB under the whole mix (a string that gives back 0.985 answers a held note at its pitch 36 dB up), so they hear it at -30. WASH (off): the plate answering the weight's listening in bars 115 and 116. By solo it is all there is above 2 kHz there, 18 dB under the weight. With it the score is 97.26 (both on 96.69): the scorer stops counting the weight's four bars as a return (2 sections of 8 return for 3, share 0.229 for 0.329) and recurrence falls to 87. Off. SCORE 99.63 on seed 0 (v5 re-read today 99.50) and 98.07 on seed 11 (v5 99.54): on that seed the scorer splits the string's listening at bar 65 into a section of its own and structure falls to 92. Nothing at bar 65 changed; the same split came and went between builds last round, and the strings move the whole song's normalising enough to tip it. So the gain is on one seed and the loss on the other is the scorer's edge, not the strings. Variety 98.5 to 99.3. FOUR BUILDS: both at -20 (not scored), both 96.69, wash only 97.26, strings only (published). WHAT IS WEAK: the strings hear only the wood, so the five of them are one colour: a held D, F and G over the tune that made them, 9 to 11 dB under the mix for sixteen bars; whether that is a halo or a drone I cannot say. The low strings never sound their own notes. 547 Hz is now 5.1 over the envelope and 749 Hz 5.0 (v5 4.6); 1.4 kHz still 7.0. THE SEAM with Hearing Things: the last bar is as loud as it was (-11.1 for -11.2) but the tail after it is now strings for four seconds (mix plan noted).
next: v7 on, every change behind a switch (v6 has sympathy on and wash off, on top of v5's flue, remember, lift, v4's three, v3's four and v2's five). (1) BY EAR when the open cards clear, one card: bars 109 to 120 of v5 beside v6 (the strings opening, dying round the weight alone, and under the groove when it comes back): a halo, or a drone that should not be there? If a drone, take 4 dB less of the wood. (2) THE STRINGS HEAR ONLY THE WOOD'S NOTES (99% of them is 500 Hz to 1 kHz): let them hear the metal as well through a low-pass at 1 kHz or the skin and the string at -36 dB, so that the low strings sound their own notes; read by sym.sh / symread.py (level by bar, the partials, the power by band) and keep 1.4 kHz out of them. (3) THE STRINGS' OWN LEAVING: they are stopped with the skin and the air in two bars; give them a turn of their own in the stopping (a section in which only the strings are let go, struck by nothing: the wood closing under them, bars 153 to 168, which is the one stopping with no mark).
